question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Beat around the bush

options.text: To avoid talking about what is important

solution: The correct answer is **Option 1)** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Beat around the bush"** means to **avoid talking about what is important.** (महत्वपूर्ण बातों से बचना) • **Example: **Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you really think. • **"To avoid talking about what is important"** means not **addressing the main point or issue directly**. (महत्वपूर्ण बातों पर बात करने से बचना) • **Example: **He kept **avoiding talking about what is important **by discussing irrelevant details. Therefore, the correct meaning of the idiom is '**To avoid talking about what is important.'** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **To talk about important things **(महत्वपूर्ण बातों के बारे में बात करना): Discussing topics that are of significance. • **Example:** We need to ***talk about important things ***like our future plans. • **To have patience **(धैर्य रखना): The ability to wait for something without getting angry or upset. • **Example:* Having patience*** is crucial when dealing with children. • **To avoid people **(लोगों से बचना): Staying away from others intentionally. • **Example:** He tends ***to avoid people*** when he is upset. 2f:Tc57, The correct answer is **Option 3)**
